sections: a solid turned cup under the girdle
each sepal is 0.84 mm at its margins and up to 1.06 along its midrib, thinning over its last fifth to a pointed tip 0.38 mm thick (a point, as the spurs' are)
a round stalk 1.2 mm across at the twig, 0.96 at the fruit
the least diameter of the wood, less a fissure's depth each side
each spur's root; past where it narrows to 0.8 mm across it is a point, listed with its run in the spurs
every petal ends in a rolled rim 0.84 mm thick and is thicker inward; heart and stamen beads are relief on it

section_sampled_diagnostic.method: inward rays from every vertex (stride shown) of the finished mesh off a crease (incident faces within 35 deg) to the first surface; spur points (radius under 0.4 mm) are reported apart
section_sampled_diagnostic.reading: Diagnostic only. A single inward ray reads relief as section: on a blossom it crosses the domed heart, a stamen bead or the rolled rim at a slant; on the wood, a fissure wall or a spur root. A sculpted blossom alone (no band) gives the same readings at its heart. The gate is the field's thinnest wall for the band and the sections by construction for every part.
